topic: What link budget trade-offs exist between RLNC overhead and forward error correction in high-PER satellite channels with strict throughput-PDR constraints?
consensus_response: In high-PER satellite channels, the optimal trade-off between RLNC overhead and FEC depends on specific link budget constraints. Increasing RLNC overhead reduces throughput due to increased packet size but may decrease PDR by distributing errors across packets. Conversely, FEC introduces latency due to retransmissions but increases link budget. Interleaving mitigates burst errors but adds latency. Adaptive Resource Allocation (ARA) can optimize trade-offs between throughput, PDR, and latency by adapting resource allocation to minimize errors and maximize link budget.
reference_context: High-PER satellite channels require consideration of varying link conditions on satellite links, including harsh channel conditions, long distance transmissions, and high speed mobility. The impact of fixed latencies on total transmission time is significant, affecting the QoS in converged satellite and terrestrial networks.
